title: "Microsoft"

One app registration in Microsoft Entra lets each person connect their own Outlook mailbox and calendar, read only, from a work, school or personal account. The same page covers Sign in with Microsoft, which is a separate registration.

**Used by:** [OpenCRM](/docs/apps/crm) for Outlook mail (the `mail.read` set).

**Ways to connect:** connect accounts, sign in.

## Connect accounts

Each person connects their own Microsoft 365 account once, in the Gateway, and every app that asks for it uses that connection. Apps never see the tokens. [How connecting works](/docs/connect-oauth)

- **Make the OAuth app here:** [entra.microsoft.com](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_RegisteredApps/ApplicationsListBlade)
- **Settings:** `MICROSOFT_365_CLIENT_ID`, `MICROSOFT_365_CLIENT_SECRET`
- **Built in:** nothing to add, only the client to set

### Redirect URI

Register this at the provider:

```text
https://<your gateway>/connect/microsoft-365/callback
```

`<your gateway>` is your Gateway's address, like `apps.example.com`.

An app that runs the sign-in itself lists its own callbacks under `redirectPaths` in its manifest entry; register those too, as `https://<app>.<your gateway><path>`. `pnpm everyapp provider show microsoft-365` prints every one.

### Make the OAuth app

1. Sign in to [Microsoft Entra → App registrations](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_RegisteredApps/ApplicationsListBlade) with an account that administers your tenant, and select **New registration**.
2. Name it (people see the name when they consent). For **Supported account types**, choose any Entra ID tenant plus personal Microsoft accounts, never single tenant.
3. Under **Redirect URI**, platform **Web**, paste the redirect URI above, and select **Register**. Copy the **Application (client) ID**.
4. Under **API permissions → Add a permission → Microsoft Graph → Delegated**, add `User.Read`, `Mail.Read` and `offline_access` (and `Calendars.Read` if an app asks for `calendar.read`).
5. Under **Certificates & secrets → New client secret**, add one (24 months at most) and copy its **Value** right away. Note the expiry date.

### Set it on your Gateway

From your EveryApp folder:

```bash
pnpm everyapp secret set MICROSOFT_365_CLIENT_ID MICROSOFT_365_CLIENT_SECRET
```

Each value goes in at a hidden prompt. Or, as an owner or admin, paste the client in **Manage workspace → Providers → Add OAuth provider**.

### Scope sets

Apps ask for named sets, never raw scopes, and the Gateway holds each app to the sets it declared.

| Set | Allows | Provider scopes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `identity` | Microsoft account (who you are) | `User.Read` |
| `mail.read` | Outlook mail (read-only) | `Mail.Read` |
| `calendar.read` | Outlook calendar (read-only) | `Calendars.Read` |

### Use it in an app

```ts
capabilities: {
  "microsoft-365": { access: "read", scopes: ["mail.read"], why: "What the app does with it." },
},
```

### Check it worked

- `pnpm everyapp provider show microsoft-365` shows the client as set, and the redirect URI.
- Open the account menu → **Connected accounts** → **Connect Microsoft 365**. You land back in the Gateway, connected.
- `pnpm everyapp provider connections` lists who has connected.

## Sign in with Microsoft

`Continue with Microsoft` on your Gateway's sign-in page, for people you've invited. It's another way into the same account. [Sign-in](/docs/sign-in)

### Make the OAuth app

1. Open [entra.microsoft.com](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_RegisteredApps/ApplicationsListBlade) and create an App registration.
2. Add the redirect URL `https://<your gateway>/api/auth/callback/microsoft`. It asks only for `openid`, `email`, `profile`: who someone is, nothing an app could act with.
3. Copy what the Gateway needs:
   - `MICROSOFT_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID`: The app registration's Application (client) ID.
   - `MICROSOFT_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET`: A client secret from Certificates & secrets (it expires; 24 months at most)

- Without MICROSOFT\_SIGNIN\_TENANT, add the optional claims `email` and `xms_edov` under Token configuration, or every sign-in is refused as unverified: any tenant's admin can put any address on their users.

Optional: `MICROSOFT_SIGNIN_TENANT`, The Directory (tenant) ID to pin sign-in to your own directory; unset means any Microsoft account (common), which then needs the xms\_edov claim.

### Turn it on

```bash
pnpm everyapp signin add microsoft
```

It asks for each value, the secret at a hidden prompt, and the button is on the sign-in page as soon as it's done.

### Check it worked

`pnpm everyapp signin show microsoft` shows each setting as set and the redirect URL. Then sign out and select the button.
